sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A SPLIT UPPER FLOW REGIME WILL EXIST OVER THE WESTERN THIRD OF THE CONUS...WITH A NORTHEASTWARD MOVING UPPER LOW OVER THE SOUTHERN ROCKIES WHILE ANOTHER UPPER LOW SLOWLY APPROACHES NORTHERN CA. MEANWHILE...ON THE SOUTHERN PERIPHERY OF A CLOSED/SLOW-MOVING UPPER TROUGH CENTERED OVER NORTHERN PORTIONS OF MANITOBA/ONTARIO...A BELT OF SEASONALLY STRONG WESTERLIES WILL CONTINUE TO OVERSPREAD THE NORTHERN PLAINS TO THE GREAT LAKES REGION.

sections.title: UPPER MIDWEST/MIDDLE MO VALLEY TO SOUTH-CENTRAL PLAINS
sections.text: A CLUSTER OF TSTMS IS EXPECTED TO BE ONGOING ACROSS PORTIONS OF THE MIDDLE MO VALLEY/UPPER MIDWEST AT THE BEGINNING OF THE PERIOD...POTENTIALLY AS FAR EAST-SOUTHEAST AS PORTIONS OF IA/PERHAPS MN. PENDING THE EXACT EVOLUTION/TIMING...A CONTINUATION/REINVIGORATION ESPECIALLY OVER THE SOUTHERNMOST CLUSTER/S CANNOT BE ENTIRELY DISCOUNTED DURING THE DAY INTO PORTIONS OF THE MIDWEST/UPPER MS VALLEY. OTHERWISE...THE BOUNDARY LAYER WILL GRADUALLY DESTABILIZE ACROSS THE MIDDLE MO VALLEY INTO THE UPPER MIDWEST/UPPER MS VALLEY ALONG/AHEAD OF A SOUTHEASTWARD-ADVANCING COLD FRONT...WITH AS MUCH AS 1500-3500 J/KG OF MLCAPE POSSIBLE. THIS WILL ESPECIALLY BE THE CASE SOUTH OF ANY EARLY DAY MCS ACTIVITY...WITH A MORE UNCERTAIN CONFIDENCE/QUANTITY OF DESTABILIZATION FARTHER NORTH NEAR THE FRONT/AN EXPECTED SURFACE LOW IN VICINITY OF NORTH-CENTRAL MN/NORTHERN WI. REGARDLESS...AIDED BY FRONTAL UPLIFT/FORCING FOR ASCENT...SURFACE BASED TSTMS ARE LIKELY TO INCREASE THROUGH MID/LATE AFTERNOON...POTENTIALLY ACROSS PORTIONS OF MN/IA INTO EASTERN/SOUTHERN NEB. MORE THAN ADEQUATE VERTICAL SHEAR WILL EXIST FOR ORGANIZED STORMS INCLUDING SUPERCELLS...CAPABLE OF SEVERE HAIL/DAMAGING WINDS AND PERHAPS A TORNADO.

sections.title: OZARKS/LOWER MS VALLEY TO SOUTHEAST STATES
sections.text: MULTIPLE CLUSTERS OF TSTMS /WITH ASSOCIATED OUTFLOW AND POSSIBLE MCV/ MAY PERSIST AND BE ONGOING ACROSS THE REGION THIS MORNING...ESPECIALLY ACROSS PARTS OF THE OZARKS/MID-SOUTH. RENEWED DIURNALLY-INTENSIFYING STORMS...AT LEAST IN AN ISOLATED/WIDELY SCATTERED SENSE...SHOULD OCCUR TO THE SOUTHEAST OF THIS EARLY DAY ACTIVITY WHERE STRONG HEATING/DESTABILIZATION OCCURS. MULTICELLULAR STORMS WITHIN AN APPRECIABLY UNSTABLE/MOIST ENVIRONMENT MAY YIELD A THREAT FOR DOWNBURSTS CAPABLE OF LOCALIZED DAMAGING WIND GUSTS AND PERHAPS PULSE-TYPE HAIL. ..GUYER/ROGERS.. 08/06/2013

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: FAIRLY DEEP CLOSED LOW WILL LINGER OVER NE MB THIS PERIOD AS A LOW-AMPLITUDE TROUGH ON ITS SW FLANK...NOW OVER MT/ND...TRACKS ESE WITHIN SEASONABLY STRONG CYCLONIC FLOW OVER THE NRN PLNS/UPR MS VLY/UPR GRT LKS. FARTHER S...A SEPARATE BAND OF SOMEWHAT ENHANCED W TO WNW FLOW WILL PREVAIL FROM THE CNTRL PLNS INTO MO AND THE LWR OH VLY...ON NRN FRINGE OF STNRY RIDGE OVER TX AND THE NWRN GULF OF MEXICO. ELSEWHERE...A VORT MAX WILL TRACK SLOWLY N ACROSS AZ...AHEAD OF A LOW/TROUGH EDGING E TOWARD THE CA CST. WITH THE EXCEPTION OF COLD FRONT NOW ENTERING ND FROM S CNTRL CANADA...AND OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES LIKELY TO BE GENERATED FROM STORMS THAT FORM LATER TODAY...SFC FEATURES WILL REMAIN WEAK. THE COLD FRONT SHOULD BECOME BETTER DEFINED AS IT ADVANCES E/SE ACROSS THE NRN PLNS/UPR MS VLY/UPR GRT LKS THROUGH THE PERIOD. POCKETS OF ENHANCED HEATING/DESTABILIZATION ALONG AND AHEAD OF THE COLD FRONT OVER THE N CNTRL STATES...AND ALONG OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES FROM OVERNIGHT STORMS FARTHER S...SHOULD SERVE AS THE MAIN CENTERS FOR STRONG TO SVR STORM DEVELOPMENT THROUGH EARLY WED AS MT/ND IMPULSE CONTINUES ESEWD.

sections.title: CNTRL PLNS INTO MID/UPR MS VLY TODAY THROUGH TNGT
sections.text: MDT WNW MID-LVL FLOW ACROSS THE NRN AND CNTRL PLNS WILL MAINTAIN DEEP EML ACROSS MUCH OF SD...NEB...WRN IA...AND KS TODAY...WHERE AMPLE MOISTURE WILL BE PRESENT TO SUPPORT STORM DEVELOPMENT AHEAD OF SE-ADVANCING COLD FRONT /ESPECIALLY ALONG AND SOUTH OF I-80/. THE GREATEST DIURNAL DESTABILIZATION...WITH MLCAPE UP TO 3000 J/KG...SHOULD OCCUR OVER CNTRL/SRN NEB AND NRN KS...S OF MORNING STORMS IN NEB AND W OF MCS NOW WEAKENING IN MO. GIVEN DEGREE OF BUOYANCY AND PRESENCE OF 25-30 KT 700-500 MB FLOW...SFC HEATING COULD YIELD CLUSTERS OF ORGANIZED/SUSTAINED STORMS WITH A RISK FOR SVR WIND AND HAIL. FARTHER N...LOW-LVL DESTABILIZATION LIKELY WILL BE MORE LIMITED CLOSER TO THE COLD FRONT AND ASSOCIATED SFC WAVE IN ERN SD/MN. NEVERTHELESS...COMBINATION OF EVEN MODEST DESTABILIZATION WITH FRONTAL UPLIFT AND FORCING FOR ASCENT PROVIDED BY PROGRESSIVE UPR IMPULSE SHOULD SUPPORT SCTD AREAS OF STORMS BY MID AFTN. THIS ACTIVITY SHOULD MOVE/DEVELOP GENERALLY EWD INTO MN...IA...AND WI BY EVE. 50 KT WLY DEEP SHEAR BENEATH AXIS OF MAIN UPR JET SUGGESTS A GOOD LIKELIHOOD FOR SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF SVR HAIL...DMGG WIND...AND PERHAPS A TORNADO. THE COMPLEX NATURE OF THE LOW-LVL PATTERN FURTHER SUGGESTS

sections.text: RENEWED STORM DEVELOPMENT SHOULD OCCUR WITH SFC HEATING TODAY IN AXIS OF HIGH PW /AOA 2 INCHES/ EXTENDING SE FROM ON-GOING MCS NOW CENTERED IN SE MO. sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: MID/HIGH LEVEL SUBTROPICAL RIDGING...NOW CENTERED OVER TEXAS...APPEARS LIKELY TO REMAIN STRONG ACROSS MUCH OF THE CENTRAL AND SOUTHERN PLAINS INTO THE SOUTHEASTERN U.S. THROUGH THIS FORECAST PERIOD. HOWEVER...FLOW IS BECOMING INCREASINGLY CYCLONIC ACROSS THE NORTHERN ROCKIES AND PLAINS...INTO THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY...TO THE SOUTH OF SIGNIFICANT CLOSED LOW CENTERED JUST SOUTHWEST OF HUDSON BAY. A COUPLE OF SHORT WAVE PERTURBATIONS ARE EMBEDDED WITHIN THIS LATTER REGIME...INCLUDING ONE SHEARED IMPULSE NOW DEVELOPING EAST SOUTHEASTWARD INTO THE DAKOTAS. THIS FEATURE IS FORECAST TO CONTINUE THROUGH THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY AND GREAT LAKES REGION LATER TODAY/TONIGHT...ACCOMPANIED BY A 50+ KT WEST NORTHWESTERLY 500 MB JET STREAK...THE SOUTHEASTWARD PROGRESSION OF A STRENGTHENING COLD FRONT ACROSS THE PLAINS/UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY...AND AT LEAST ONE WEAK FRONTAL WAVE ACROSS CENTRAL MINNESOTA INTO NORTHWEST WISCONSIN LATE THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING. WHILE A NORTHWARD RETURN OF LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE FROM THE MIDDLE MISSOURI VALLEY IS EXPECTED AHEAD OF THE FRONT TODAY...HIGHER MOISTURE CONTENT AIR CHARACTERIZED BY SURFACE DEW POINTS IN THE 70S AND PRECIPITABLE WATER NEAR 2 INCHES LI

sections.title: UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY INTO MID MISSOURI VALLEY
sections.text: WITH STEEPENING MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES...PRE-FRONTAL MOISTENING IS EXPECTED TO BE SUFFICIENT TO SUPPORT MODERATELY LARGE CAPE BY LATE AFTERNOON. COUPLED WITH THE STRENGTHENING DEEP LAYER SHEAR ...THE ENVIRONMENT WILL BECOME CONDUCIVE TO SEVERE STORM DEVELOPMENT WITHIN THE WARM SECTOR OF THE SURFACE WAVE...SOUTHWESTWARD ALONG THE DEVELOPING SURFACE FRONT. CONFIDENCE IS HIGHEST THAT THIS WILL OCCUR ROUGHLY FROM PARTS OF CENTRAL MINNESOTA INTO NORTHEASTERN NEBRASKA...ON THE NORTHERN EDGE OF THE WARMER MID-LEVEL AIR...BEFORE SPREADING SOUTHEASTWARD INTO WESTERN WISCONSIN AND NORTHERN/WESTERN IOWA THIS EVENING. A FEW SUPERCELLS ARE POSSIBLE INITIALLY...AND LOW-LEVEL HODOGRAPHS ACROSS EAST CENTRAL MINNESOTA INTO WEST CENTRAL WISCONSIN MAY BECOME STRONG ENOUGH TO SUPPORT A RISK FOR TORNADOES. OTHERWISE ...THE EVOLUTION OF ONE OR MORE ORGANIZED MESOSCALE CONVECTIVE SYSTEMS APPEARS POSSIBLE...ACCOMPANIED BY THE RISK FOR SEVERE WINDS AND HAIL...BEFORE DIMINISHING OVERNIGHT.

sections.title: UPPER/MIDDLE MS VALLEY
sections.text: PER WATER VAPOR IMAGERY...PRIMARY IMPULSE/MID-LEVEL SPEED MAX APPEARS TO BE SPREADING EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD ACROSS CENTRAL MN EARLY THIS EVENING. AHEAD OF A WEAK SURFACE LOW AND PRE-FRONTAL TROUGH/TRAILING COLD FRONT...ONGOING SEMI-DISCRETE/SUPERCELLULAR STORMS ARE LIKELY TO PERSIST EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD WHILE GRADUALLY MERGING INTO LINE SEGMENTS INTO WI/EVENTUALLY MI THE REMAINDER OF THE NIGHT. BOUTS OF SEVERE HAIL/DAMAGING WINDS WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE. OTHER AT LEAST WIDELY SCATTERED TSTMS ARE LIKELY TO PERSIST AT LEAST FOR A TIME THIS EVENING WITHIN A MODERATE TO STRONGLY UNSTABLE ENVIRONMENT /00Z SOUNDINGS FROM OMAHA AND DAVENPORT IA/ ALONG A LOW-LEVEL CONFLUENCE ZONE FROM EASTERN NEB INTO SOUTHERN IA/EVENTUALLY NORTHERN IL. DAMAGING WINDS/SEVERE HAIL ARE THE PRIMARY HAZARDS.

sections.title: SOUTH-CENTRAL PLAINS TO LOWER MO VALLEY/OZARKS
sections.text: AN ONGOING LOOSE CLUSTER OF STORMS ACROSS SOUTHWEST KS/NORTHWEST OK MAY PERSIST GENERALLY EASTWARD TONIGHT WITH AID OF AN INCREASING LOW LEVEL JET...WITH OTHER STORMS POTENTIALLY FORMING ACROSS THE LOWER MO VALLEY/OZARKS WITHIN A WARM ADVECTION REGIME. AT LEAST ISOLATED DAMAGING WINDS/SEVERE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE. ..GUYER.. 08/07/2013

mesoscale_discussions.summary: WHILE A STRONG WIND GUST CANNOT BE RULED OUT...TRENDS IN RADAR IMAGERY AND DECREASING LIGHTNING STRIKES WITH THE CLUSTER OF STORMS IN ERN NEB/SWRN IA SUGGEST THE SEVERE WEATHER THREAT IS DIMINISHING.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AT 14Z...OBSERVATIONAL DATA INDICATED AN OUTFLOW BOUNDARY ATTENDANT TO THE CLUSTER OF STORMS IN ERN NEB/SWRN IA HAS MOVED SOUTH OF THE STRONGER REFLECTIVITY...WITH THIS BOUNDARY EXTENDING FROM EXTREME SWRN IA WSWWD INTO SOUTH CENTRAL NEB. AREA WSR-88D VAD WINDS FROM SRN NEB TO CENTRAL IA SHOWED A RELATIVE LACK OF INFLOW TO THE ONGOING STORMS IN THIS REGION...WITH LOW LEVEL WINDS OBSERVED FROM THE N/NW. THESE TRENDS AND LIMITED REMAINING FORCING FOR ASCENT OVER ERN NEB/SWRN IA THIS MORNING VERIFY THE DECREASE IN LIGHTNING ACTIVITY...WARMING CLOUD TOPS AND THE WEAKENING TREND IN 7 KM AND 9 KM CAPPI DATA. GIVEN THESE OBSERVATIONS...A NEW WW IS NOT WARRANTED DOWNSTREAM OF THE CURRENT SVR TSTM WATCH.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO CONTINUE INCREASING IN COVERAGE OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS...WITH A FEW STRONGER CELLS BECOMING CAPABLE OF PRODUCING MARGINAL HAIL/WIND. WW IS NOT EXPECTED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY SHOWS FAIRLY EXTENSIVE CLOUD COVER ACROSS MUCH OF TN...WHICH HAS HINDERED DESTABILIZATION IN MOST AREAS. FARTHER S INTO MS/AL HOWEVER...MORE SUBSTANTIAL DIURNAL HEATING COMBINED WITH A VERY MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER /LOW TO MID 70S DEWPOINTS/ HAS YIELDED MODERATE INSTABILITY /MIXED-LAYER CAPE CURRENTLY IN THE 2000 TO 3000 J/KG RANGE/. THIS DESTABILIZATION HAS SUPPORTED AN INCREASE IN THUNDERSTORMS ON THE SOUTHEASTERN FRINGE OF THE REMNANT MCS CROSSING THE MID MS/LOWER OH/TN VALLEYS THIS AFTERNOON...AND EXPECT STORMS TO CONTINUE EXPANDING IN COVERAGE OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. DESPITE INCREASING STORM COVERAGE AND FAVORABLE MOISTURE/INSTABILITY...DEEP-LAYER WIND FIELD REMAINS MODEST -- GENERALLY UNSUPPORTIVE OF A WELL-ORGANIZED SEVERE THREAT. STILL...WITH SHEAR LIKELY SUFFICIENT FOR WEAK MULTICELL ORGANIZATION...A FEW STRONGER STORMS/STORM CLUSTERS MAY BECOME CAPABLE OF MARGINAL HAIL AND/OR LOCALLY GUSTY WINDS CAPABLE OF LOW-END WIND DAMAGE THROUGH THE REMAINDER OF THE AFTERNOON AS CONVECTION SHIFTS SEWD WITH TIME.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: CONVECTIVE AND ENVIRONMENTAL TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED FOR POTENTIAL WATCH ISSUANCE THIS AFTERNOON ACROSS MUCH OF CENTRAL AND PARTS OF SRN MN INTO WRN WI.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: TRENDS IN OBSERVATIONAL DATA/OBJECTIVE ANALYSES INTO EARLY THIS AFTERNOON INDICATED THE ENVIRONMENT IS DESTABILIZING IN THE WAKE OF MORNING CLOUDINESS ACROSS CENTRAL/SRN MN AND WRN WI. 17Z SURFACE ANALYSIS SHOWED AN AREA OF LOW PRESSURE HAD SHIFTED ESEWD TO ALONG THE SERN ND/WEST CENTRAL MN BORDER...WHILE A WARM FRONT EXTENDED ESEWD JUST SOUTHWEST OF THE I-94 CORRIDOR TO THE SRN TWIN CITIES METRO INTO CENTRAL WI. S/SWLY LOW LEVEL WINDS HAVE DEVELOPED FROM ERN NEB INTO CENTRAL MN PER WSR-88D VAD WINDS AIDING IN MOISTURE RETURN TO THE WARM SECTOR WHERE SURFACE HEATING WILL PERSIST THROUGH THE AFTERNOON. THIS COMBINED WITH MIDLEVEL COOLING/STEEPENING MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES AS A TROUGH AND THE EXIT REGION OF 50 KT WLY MIDLEVEL JET ADVANCE INTO THE UPPER MS VALLEY WILL SUPPORT FURTHER DESTABILIZATION WITH MLCAPE TO AROUND 1500 J/KG LIKELY ALONG AND SOUTH OF THE WARM FRONT. AS THE SURFACE LOW TRACKS EAST REACHING NWRN WI BY THIS EVENING...THE WARM FRONT SHOULD ADVANCE NWD THROUGH THE TWIN CITIES METRO INTO NWRN WI. EARLY AFTERNOON VISIBLE IMAGERY SHOWED CU CONTINUING TO FORM INVOF THE SURFACE LOW AND WARM FRONT...AND ALSO SWD ALONG A PRE-FRONTAL TROUGH TO THE N OF KRWF. LAST SEVERAL RUNS OF THE HRRR HAVE BEEN CONSISTENT WITH STORMS FORMING NEAR THE SURFACE LOW BETWEEN 20-21Z AND SPREADING EWD TO THE TWIN CITIES BY 23Z. SATELLITE IMAGERY SHOWED A W-E ORIENTED CLOUDS OVER SD WITH THIS FEATURE LIKELY ATTENDANT TO THE 50+ KT WLY MIDLEVEL JET NOW NOSING INTO CENTRAL/SRN MN. EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR OF 40-50 KT AS MIDLEVEL WINDS STRENGTHEN OVER MN TO WRN WI INTO THE EVENING ATOP VERTICALLY VEERING LOW-MID LEVEL WINDS SUGGESTS SUPERCELLS WILL BE A LIKELY STORM MODE. HENCE...ALL SEVERE TYPES CAN BE EXPECTED WITH THE TORNADO THREAT GREATEST INVOF THE WARM FRONT WHERE LOW LEVEL SHEAR WILL B

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A WW MAY BE NEEDED THIS AFTERNOON INTO THE EVENING ACROSS SWRN-SRN KS AND ADJACENT PARTS OF NRN OK. HAIL AND STRONG WIND GUSTS ARE EXPECTED TO BE THE GREATEST THREATS WITH THE STRONGER STORMS IN THIS REGION. THIS REGION WILL BE MONITORED FOR ADDITIONAL STORM DEVELOPMENT AND UPSCALE GROWTH THAT WOULD WARRANT THE NEED FOR A WATCH.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AT 20Z...RADAR IMAGERY SHOWED A STRONG-SVR TSTM LOCATED ALONG THE CO/KS BORDER AREA /SERN CHEYENNE COUNTY CO AND ADJACENT PARTS OF WALLACE/GREELEY COUNTIES KS/. MEANWHILE...ADDITIONAL CU/TCU AND CB/S WERE DEVELOPING ALONG A NE-SW ORIENTED BOUNDARY IN THE TX PANHANDLE...WITH CU/TCU DEVELOPING OVER SERN CO. SURFACE ANALYSIS ALSO SHOWED A MORE PROMINENT BOUNDARY EXTENDING FROM NWRN AR THROUGH NERN OK TO FAR SOUTH CENTRAL KS...AND THEN SWWD INTO NWRN OK AND THE FAR NRN TX PANHANDLE. STRONG SURFACE HEATING AND SURFACE DEWPOINTS IN THE UPPER 60S TO LOWER 70S F EITHER SIDE OF THE LATTER SURFACE FEATURE BENEATH STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES ARE RESULTING IN A MODERATELY-STRONGLY UNSTABLE AIR MASS. ALTHOUGH BULK SHEAR IS RELATIVELY WEAKER THAN LOCATIONS FARTHER N...MAGNITUDES OF 25-35 KT SUGGEST BOTH MULTICELLS AND A FEW SUPERCELLS WILL BE POSSIBLE. MODELS HAVE REMAINED CONSISTENT SHOWING STORMS DEVELOPING AND INCREASING IN COVERAGE ACROSS SWRN KS BETWEEN 22-00Z AS A MIDLEVEL IMPULSE EMBEDDED WITHIN THE MONSOONAL MOISTURE PLUME TRACKS FROM NRN NM/SRN CO INTO THE KS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: CONDITIONAL SVR POTENTIAL IS INCREASING OVER DISCUSSION AREA...ESPECIALLY FROM NERN NEB EWD ACROSS PORTIONS W-CENTRAL/NWRN IA. TSTMS MAY DEVELOP AND EVOLVE UPSCALE WITH INITIALLY MIXED WIND/HAIL THREAT...EVOLVING MORE TOWARD WIND WITH TIME. CONVECTIVE TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED FOR POSSIBLE WW.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SFC MESOANALYSIS SHOWS LEADING COLD FRONT EXTENDING FROM SFC LOW OVER N-CENTRAL MN SSWWD ACROSS SWRN MN...EXTREME SERN SD TO NEAR ODX-LBF-OGA LINE. THIS BOUNDARY WILL CONTINUE TO MOVE SEWD ACROSS THIS REGION THROUGH EVENING...WITH SECONDARY/REINFORCING FRONT FARTHER N ACROSS NERN THROUGH S-CENTRAL SD. VIS IMAGERY SHOWS PACK OF ENHANCED SHALLOW CONVECTION FROM ERN PORTIONS NEB SANDHILLS EWD TO DEEPER TOWERS OVER PORTIONS ANTELOPE/MADISON/PIERCE COUNTIES NEB...NEAR FRONT. THIS AREA REPRESENTS GREATEST PROBABILITY FOR GENESIS OF LONGSTANDING CONVECTION...BEING NEAR N EDGE OF MOST FAVORABLE THERMODYNAMIC CHARACTERISTICS. RICHEST PREFRONTAL THETAE IS EVIDENT S OF LONGITUDE OF SUX...WHERE SFC DEW POINTS UPPER 60S TO LOW 70S F ARE COMMON...CONTRIBUTING TO MLCAPE 2000-4000 J/KG FROM WRN IA ACROSS ERN/SRN NEB. EXTENT OF BACKBUILDING ACROSS CENTRAL/SRN NEB IS UNCERTAIN...GIVEN PRESENCE OF WEAK CINH...BUT ALSO FRONTAL COL OVER S-CENTRAL/SWRN NEB WITH ACCOMPANYING RELATIVE MIN IN BOUNDARY-FORCED LIFT. LIMITING FACTOR FOR RAPID/ROBUST DEVELOPMENT FARTHER NE MAY BE PRESENCE OF WEAK AND SUBSTANTIALLY VEERED SFC FLOW -- AVERAGING WLY AT 5-10 KT...WHICH WILL HAMPER BOTH FRONTAL CONVERGENCE AND STORM-RELATIVE INFLOW. AS SUCH...SUSTENANCE OF ANY DEEP CONVECTION THAT DOES DEVELOP IS IN QUESTION...DESPITE PRESENCE OF FAVORABLE CAPE AND WEAK CAPPING FOR ANOTHER FEW HOURS. DESPITE THAT WEAK/VEERED SFC FLOW...STG MIDLEVEL WINDS YIELD EFFECTIVE SHEAR MAGNITUDES 40-50 KT IN FCST SOUNDINGS...DERIVED ALMOST ENTIRELY FROM SPEED SHEAR. THIS MAY AID IN ORGANIZATION OF ANY CONVECTION THAT CAN LAST AND GROW UPSCALE.

SEPARATE/MORE DIFFUSE CONFLUENCE LINE WAS DRAWN FROM BOONE COUNTY AND NRN OMA SUBURBS. WIDELY SCATTERED TCU/CB WAS EVIDENT ALONG AND BETWEEN THESE BOUNDARIES...IN THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED BY SFC DEW POINTS UPPER 60S TO 70S F...AND MLCAPE GENERALLY 1500-2500 J/KG IN MODIFIED RR SOUNDINGS. THOUGH CONFLUENT...SFC FLOW ALSO IS WEAK...GENERALLY 5-10 KT ACROSS MOST OF THIS AREA...WHICH WILL LIMIT CONVERGENCE...STORM-RELATIVE INFLOW AND HODOGRAPH SIZE. DESPITE WEAK SFC WINDS...SPEED INCREASE WITH HEIGHT IS STRONG ENOUGH TO YIELD 40-45 KT EFFECTIVE SHEAR MAGNITUDE...SUPPORTING SOME ORGANIZATION POTENTIAL WITH ANY SUSTAINED TSTMS. REF SPC MESOSCALE DISCUSSION 1640 FOR COVERAGE OF MORE IMMEDIATELY PREFRONTAL SVR POTENTIAL NW AND W OF THIS REGIME.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SVR POTENTIAL IS FCST TO SPREAD SEWD ACROSS REMAINDER WW THROUGH EVENING...AND MAY 1. PERSIST OVER PORTIONS WW AREA PAST SCHEDULED 02Z EXPIRATION AND/OR 2. SHIFT E OF INITIAL WW OVER PORTIONS WRN WI AS WELL. AS SUCH...ADDITIONAL OR REPLACEMENT WW MAY BE REQUIRED BY ABOUT 130Z. WW MAY BE CLEARED BEHIND COLD-POOL FEATURE DISCUSSED BELOW...MOVING SEWD INTO WRN MN.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SFC MESOANALYSIS SHOWED SFC LOW OVER N-CENTRAL MN...SOMEWHAT MUDDLED BY SURROUNDING CONVECTION...ACCOMPANIED BY TWO COLD FRONTAL SEGMENTS. LEADING FRONT EXTENDED SSWWD ACROSS SWRN MN AND EXTREME NWRN IA INTO NERN NEB...CHARACTERIZED BY WIND SHIFT AND ONLY MINOR CHANGES IN THETAE. SECONDARY/STRONGER FRONTAL SURGE WAS EVIDENT OVER W-CENTRAL MN SWWD ACROSS S-CENTRAL SD. SEVERAL TSTMS THAT INITIATED BEHIND SECOND FRONT HAVE CAUGHT THAT BOUNDARY OVER WRN MN...WHILE ISOLATED SVR TSTM WAS EVIDENT ALONG LEADING FRONT OVER MEEKER COUNTY. MEANWHILE...LARGER CLUSTER OF POSTFRONTAL TSTMS WAS MOVING SEWD FROM EXTREME SERN ND AND NERN SD...ACCOMPANIED BY WELL-DEVELOPED COLD POOL WITH OUTFLOW ARC EXTENDING WSWWD ACROSS ABR AREA. SCATTERED TSTMS -- SOME SVR -- ALSO HAVE FORMED ALONG WARM FRONT EXTENDING FROM LOW ESEWD OVER CENTRAL WI. UPSCALE GROWTH OF CONVECTION ACROSS WW AREA MAY OCCUR AS COLD POOL CATCHES UP TO AND ABSORBS PRECURSORY CONVECTION OVER WRN/CENTRAL MN. INITIAL SUPERCELLULAR THREAT OF LARGE HAIL...ISOLATED DAMAGING WIND AND A TORNADO OR TWO THEN WOULD EVOLVE INTO PREDOMINANT WIND POTENTIAL WITH SEWD TO ESEWD-MOVING/FORWARD-PROPAGATIONAL MCS...LIKELY FOCUSED ALONG AND S OF WARM FRONT. PRECONVECTIVE AIR MASS NEAR COLD FRONTS GENERALLY IS CHARACTERIZED BY 60S F SFC DEW POINTS...WITH MLCAPE LIKELY TO DIMINISH SLOWLY FROM PRESENT 1000-1500 J/KG VALUES. HOWEVER...FARTHER E ACROSS SERN MN AND WI...SWLY FLOW WILL CONTINUE REGIME OF MOISTURE ADVECTION...RENDERING AIR MASS MORE FAVORABLY MOIST WITH TIME AND HELPING TO MAINTAIN AT LEAST MRGL BUOYANCY. REF SPC MESOSCALE DISCUSSIONS 1640 AND 1641 FOR NOWCAST DETAILS ON AREAS S AND SW OF WW. ..EDWARDS.. 08/06/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: LARGE HAIL AND A FEW DMGG WIND GUSTS WILL CONTINUE TO BE THE PRIMARY THREAT THROUGH THE NEXT 1-2 HRS OVER AND JUST S OF WW 475. NUMEROUS CELL INTERACTIONS/MERGERS COULD EVENTUALLY LEAD TO CONSOLIDATION INTO AN ORGANIZED COLD POOL LATER THIS EVENING...AND SUBSEQUENTLY...AN INCREASING DMGG WIND THREAT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SFC MESOANALYSIS SHOWS A WEAKLY CONVERGENT BOUNDARY EXTENDING WSW-ENE FROM THE NERN TX PANHANDLE INTO NWRN OK. CONVECTION HAS BECOME MORE ROBUST WITHIN THE PAST TWO HRS INVOF THIS BOUNDARY AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER HAS BECOME HOT/WELL MIXED OVER THE ERN TX PANHANDLE. MORE ORGANIZED CONVECTION WAS NOTED FARTHER N ACROSS THE OK PANHANDLE AND SWRN KS...GIVEN MORE FAVORABLE SHEAR PARAMETERS WITH NEAR 30 KT OF MIDLEVEL FLOW AND MOIST E-SELY SFC WINDS N OF THE BOUNDARY. REPORTS OF VERY LARGE HAIL HAVE BEEN RECEIVED IN ASSOCIATION WITH A LONGER-LIVED SUPERCELL MOVING INTO HASKELL AND SEWARD COUNTIES KS AS OF 2330Z. WITH INCREASING AREAL COVERAGE OF CONVECTION NOTED MORE RECENTLY...ADDITIONAL STORM SPLITS AND CELL MERGERS COULD CONTRIBUTE TO A CONSOLIDATING LINE/COLD POOL INTO THE EVENING HRS. LATEST HIGH-RESOLUTION MODEL GUIDANCE /E.G. HRRR/ SUPPORTS THIS SCENARIO...AND SUPPORTS A CONVECTIVE LINE PROPAGATING EWD INVOF THE SFC BOUNDARY. SHOULD THIS OCCUR...THE DMGG WIND THREAT WILL PROBABLY INCREASE INTO PARTS OF NWRN OK AND S-CNTRL KS. ..ROGERS.. 08/06/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: CLUSTER OF TSTMS MOVING ACROSS SWRN KS AND NWRN OK IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE PROGRESSING EWD. GIVEN A SLIGHT INCREASE IN UPDRAFT INTENSITY RECENTLY NOTED...A DMGG WIND THREAT MAY EXTEND E INTO SERN KS...WHICH WILL LIKELY REQUIRE ISSUANCE OF A WW.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RADAR TRENDS SHOW RELATIVELY UNORGANIZED TSTM CLUSTER OVER SWRN/S-CNTRL KS MOVING EWD AROUND 20 KT. MORE RECENTLY...SOME SIGNS OF UPDRAFT INTENSIFICATION HAVE BEEN NOTED...PERHAPS AIDED BY A MODEST STRENGTHENING OF LLJ AND ASSOCIATED WARM ADVECTION ATOP A QUASISTATIONARY W-E BOUNDARY. RAP OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS SUGGESTS AMPLE LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE AND INSTABILITY DOWNSTREAM...WITH MUCAPE VALUES LIKELY EXCEEDING 4000 J/KG. THE COMBINATION OF A MOIST AND VERY UNSTABLE AIR MASS...ALONG WITH AROUND 20 KT OF MEAN TROPOSPHERIC FLOW...WILL BE SUPPORTIVE FOR TSTMS PERSISTING EWD FOR THE NEXT SEVERAL HRS...AND A POSSIBLE DMGG WIND THREAT SHOULD CONVECTION CONTINUE TO INTENSIFY AND BECOME MORE ORGANIZED.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SVR HAIL/GUST THREAT CONTINUES OVER MAINLY SRN PORTIONS WW. PER COORD W/AFFECTED WFOS...SOME NRN COUNTIES MAY BE CLEARED SHORTLY...WHERE AIR MASS HAS BEEN AND WILL BE STABILIZED SUBSTANTIALLY BY COMBINED EFFECTS OF CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW AND/OR DIABATIC SFC COOLING. ISOLATED SVR MAY OCCUR N OF WW FROM CONVECTION OVER NRN IA...OR FROM TSTMS CURRENTLY OVER SERN NEB JUST S OF WW...AND POTENTIALLY AFFECTING NEARBY PORTIONS MO/KS. HOWEVER...OVERALL THREAT APPEARS TO BE GETTING MORE ISOLATED/DISORGANIZED AREA-WIDE. DEPENDING ON CONVECTIVE TRENDS...MORE OF WW MAY BE CLEARED BEFORE SCHEDULED 05Z EXPIRATION.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: MOST OF WW REMAINS AHEAD OF WEAK/SLOW-MOVING SFC COLD FRONT ESTIMATED FROM S-CENTRAL MN SWWD ACROSS SUX/DVN/IML AREAS. OUTFLOW BOUNDARY FROM EARLIER SVR TSTM APPEARS TO BE ENHANCING LIFT FOR LATER TSTMS MOVING SEWD FROM PLATTE COUNTY NEB. TSTM OUTFLOW AND/OR DOWNSHEAR PRECIP HAS STABILIZED BOUNDARY LAYER OVER MUCH OF I-80 CORRIDOR FROM DSM AREA EWD...AND OVER AREAS NW THROUGH E OF OTM-AREA CONVECTION. S AND W OF THAT ACTIVITY...PORTIONS SRN IA AND SERN NEB REMAIN IN FAVORABLY UNSTABLE PRECONVECTIVE ENVIRONMENT. RICH BOUNDARY-LAYER MOISTURE...WITH SFC DEW POINTS UPPER 60S TO LOW 70S F...WILL MAINTAIN ONLY SLOW RATE OF SFC COOLING AND CINH INCREASE...KEEPING EFFECTIVE LIFTED PARCELS SFC-BASED FOR 2-3 MORE HOURS AND MLCAPE AOA 2000 J/KG. GIVEN 40-50 KT EFFECTIVE SHEAR MAGNITUDES...ANY SUSTAINED CONVECTION STILL MAY ACQUIRE SUPERCELLULAR CHARACTERISTICS...THOUGH WEAKNESS OF NEAR-SFC WINDS WILL CONTINUE TO LIMIT HODOGRAPH SIZE. ..EDWARDS.. 08/07/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: WW SHOULD BE CONTINUED ALONG/AHEAD OF PRIMARY MCS. SVR HAIL STILL IS POSSIBLE...BUT RISK APPEARS TO BE WEIGHING MORE STRONGLY TOWARD WIND WITH TIME AS BROADER TSTM COMPLEX GRADUALLY GETS BETTER ORGANIZED. ANOTHER WW MAY BE REQUIRED DOWNSHEAR ACROSS WI.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: OUTFLOW FROM SEVERAL AREAS OF CONVECTION ACROSS WRN WI AND SERN MN IS AGGREGATING INTO SINGLE COLD POOL WITH STG-SVR CONVECTION ON BOTH SIDES OF ITS LEADING EDGE...AND INCREASING TSTM COVERAGE OVERALL. SFC ANALYSIS SHOWED WARM FRONT EXTENDING FROM CHIPPEWA/TAYLOR COUNTIES WI ESEWD ACROSS GRB AREA...AND DRIFTING NEWD. ALTHOUGH SFC DIABATIC COOLING IS EXPECTED TO STRENGTHEN MLCINH AHEAD OF THIS ACTIVITY...NEAR-SFC MOIST ADVECTION WILL MAKE THAT PROCESS GRADUAL. FORCED ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH FORWARD-PROPAGATING MCS COLD POOL...AND ENHANCED AMIDST DOWNWARD MOMENTUM TRANSFER FROM BELT OF 50-KT MIDLEVEL FLOW...MAY BE SUFFICIENT TO OFFSET SHALLOW LAYER OF RELATIVELY STABLE NEAR-SFC AIR AND SPREAD DAMAGING-WIND THREAT ACROSS CENTRAL/ERN WI. SWD BACKBUILDING OF TSTM COMPLEX IS UNCERTAIN ...BUT MAY AFFECT PORTIONS EXTREME NERN IA AND SWRN/S-CENTRAL WI AS WELL. WEAK-MDT BUOYANCY WILL BE AVAILABLE WITH MLCAPE AND MUCAPE EACH IN 500-1200 J/KG ACROSS THIS CORRIDOR...BASED ON MODIFICATIONS TO MPX/GRB RAOB AND MODIFIED MODEL SOUNDINGS. EFFECTIVE SHEAR VECTORS OF AROUND 50 KT ARE ALIGNED NEARLY PARALLEL TO WARM FRONT...WHICH SHOULD BE IN NRN PORTION OF MOST PROBABLE MCS-PROPAGATION CORRIDOR. ..EDWARDS.. 08/07/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED LARGE HAIL/DAMAGING GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE THE NEXT FEW HOURS WITH A SMALL STORM CLUSTER MOVING INTO SW NEB...BUT THE NEED FOR A WATCH IS UNCLEAR.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STORMS THAT FORMED EARLIER THIS EVENING IN AN UPSLOPE FLOW REGIME ACROSS THE NEB PANHANDLE CONTINUE TO MOVE SEWD TOWARD SW NEB...WITH THE RECENT INTENSIFICATION OF A STORM NEAR SNY. THIS CONVECTION WILL LIKELY CONTINUE TO MOVE SEWD ON THE IMMEDIATE COOL SIDE OF A SWD-MOVING COLD FRONT...WITHIN A CORRIDOR OF MODERATE INSTABILITY THAT WAS PREVIOUSLY SAMPLED BY THE 00Z LBF SOUNDING. THOUGH LARGE-SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT IS WEAK...THE PRESENCE OF WEAK LOW-LEVEL ASCENT ALONG THE SURFACE FRONT...AND INTERACTIONS BETWEEN THE FRONT AND STORM-SCALE OUTFLOW...WILL HELP SUSTAIN THE STORMS FOR A FEW MORE HOURS. MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES...BUOYANCY...AND DEEP-LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR ARE SUFFICIENT FOR SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING GUSTS. HOWEVER...THE COVERAGE OF SEVERE STORMS IS IN QUESTION AND THE AREA POTENTIALLY IMPACTED IS FAIRLY SMALL...SO THE NEED FOR A WATCH IS NOT CLEAR. ..THOMPSON.. 08/07/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: WI SQLN WITH EMBEDDED LEWPS/BOWING STRUCTURES IS NEARING THE WRN SHORE OF LK MI. CONVECTIVE SYSTEM MAY REMAIN STRONG TO SVR AS IT CONTINUES E ACROSS THE LK AND INTO PARTS OF LWR MI LATER THIS MORNING...NECESSITATING ISSUANCE OF A WATCH.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: NE-SW SQLN WITH EMBEDDED LEWPS OVER CNTRL/ERN WI IS MOVING E AT APPROXIMATELY 55 KTS. THE CONVECTIVE SYSTEM IS BEING SUPPORTED BY ASCENT AHEAD OF NW WI VORT MAX AND ASSOCIATED 50-60 KT MID-LVL JET STREAK. THE DOWNSTREAM LOW-LVL ENVIRONMENT LIKELY IS NOT QUITE AS CONDUCIVE TO DOWNSTREAM MCS PROPAGATION/MCS SUSTENANCE AS WAS WI EARLIER THIS EVE...DUE TO CLOUDS THAT COVERED MUCH OF LWR MI TUE AFTN. NEVERTHELESS...AMPLE MOISTURE /PW AROUND 1.25 INCHES AND SFC DEWPOINTS IN THE MID 60S F/ IS IN PLACE TO SUPPORT NEW STORM DEVELOPMENT GIVEN PRESENCE OF A WELL-DEFINED MCS GUST FRONT --- AS IS NOW PRESENT IN WI. WITH THE WI UPR IMPULSE EXPECTED TO CONTINUE STEADILY EWD...AND WITH ASSOCIATED BELT OF STRENGTHENING DEEP WLY FLOW EXPECTED TO OVERSPREAD LWR MI IN TANDEM WITH THE MCS...IT APPEARS THAT A BETTER-THAN-EVEN CHANCE WILL EXIST FOR AT LEAST LOCALLY DMGG WINDS. A WW MAY BE NEEDED FOR PARTS OF WRN LWR MI IN THE NEXT HOUR.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STRONG TO POSSIBLY SVR TSTMS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE MOVING/DEVELOPING E/NE FROM WW 478 INTO NRN AND ERN KS AND PERHAPS INTO PARTS OF WRN/CNTRL MO...POSSIBLY REQUIRING WW ISSUANCE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: TSTMS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE FORMING ON LEADING /ERN AND NERN/ EDGE OF COLD POOL ASSOCIATED WITH KS MCS. DEEP EML AND RICH LOW-LVL MOISTURE SUGGEST SOME POTENTIAL FOR ADDITIONAL PRECIP-ENHANCED LOCALLY-DMGG SFC WINDS AS THE COLD POOL/GUST FRONT CONTINUE TO EXPAND ENE INTO ENVIRONMENT OF 30 KT WNWLY DEEP SHEAR AND STRONG MID-LVL BUOYANCY /PER 00Z WED TOP RAOB/. OTHER STORMS MAY FORM AHEAD OF GUST FRONT AS LOW-LVL UPLIFT INCREASES ALONG AND S OF WEAK COLD FRONT NOW EDGING SEWD ACROSS TOWARD FAR NW MO --- AND ALONG W-E WAA ZONE INTO CNTRL MO. OVERALL SETUP MAY REQUIRE WW ISSUANCE IN THE NEXT HOUR GIVEN POTENTIAL FOR LOCALLY DMGG WIND AND POSSIBLY SVR HAIL.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: TSTMS...INCLUDING A FEW THAT OCCASIONALLY MAY BECOME SVR...EXPECTED TO PERSIST OVER SRN/ERN IA. THIS ACTIVITY MAY SPREAD INTO NRN MO AND NW IL LATER THIS MORNING. AREA MAY REQUIRE WW ISSUANCE IF ACTIVITY STRENGTHENS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SCTD TSTMS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE FORMING ALONG AND AHEAD OF WEAK WSW-ENE COLD FRONT EDGING SLOWLY SE ACROSS SRN IA THIS MORNING. AREA AHEAD OF THE FRONT IS CHARACTERIZED BY CONSIDERABLE LOW-TO MID-LVL BUOYANCY GIVEN REGIONAL 00Z RAOBS...WITH MUCAPE LIKELY AOA 2500 J/KG ABOVE SHALLOW...NOCTURNAL...SFC-BASED STABLE LAYER. MODERATE...DEEP WLY FLOW WILL PERSIST ACROSS THE REGION...WITH 30-40 KT 700-500 MB FLOW OVER CNTRL IA DECREASING TO ABOUT 25 KT IN NRN MO...YIELDING 40+ KT WLY DEEP SHEAR. FORCING FOR ASCENT SHOULD REMAIN SLIGHTLY POSITIVE FOR THE NEXT FEW HOURS AS AREA IS GLANCED BY SRN FRINGE OF SEASONABLY STRONG DISTURBANCE MOVING E ACROSS WI. LOW-LVL UPLIFT WILL...HOWEVER...LIKELY REMAIN LIMITED AS CURRENT AND NEAR-TERM SFC FORECASTS SHOW NOTHING TO SUGGEST AN INCREASE IN WIND SPEEDS/CONVERGENCE. THE OVERALL SETUP APPEARS TO BE ONE THAT COULD RESULT IN OCCASIONAL SUSTAINED STORMS AND POSSIBLY A FEW TRANSIENT SUPERCELLS. THESE COULD YIELD ISOLD INSTANCES OF SVR HAIL AND/OR LOCALLY DMGG WIND. A WW MIGHT BE REQUIRED IF THE ACTIVITY SHOWS A MARKED INCREASE IN STORM STRENGTH AND/OR COVERAGE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: TSTMS WILL CONTINUE THROUGH LATER THIS MORNING OVER CNTRL AND SRN LWR MI. ISOLD SVR WIND GUSTS MAY OCCUR...BUT A NEW WW IS NOT ANTICIPATED ATTM.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SQLN HAS SWEPT E ACROSS THE NRN HALF OF LWR MI IN THE PAST SEVERAL HOURS...ACCOMPANIED BY SCTD INSTANCES OF STRONG TO SVR SFC WINDS. THE SYSTEM COLD POOL HAS ELONGATED ROUGHLY W-E ACROSS NRN AND CNTRL LWR MI...PARALLEL TO THE SEASONABLY STRONG...DEEP WLY FLOW. UPLIFT ALONG THE DOWNSHEAR /ERN/ SIDE OF THE COLD POOL SHOULD ALLOW THE SQLN TO CONTINUE E ACROSS LK HURON OVER THE NEXT TWO HOURS. THE STORMS SHOULD...HOWEVER...WEAKEN AS THEY MOVE INTO A LOW-LVL ENVIRONMENT INCREASINGLY HOSTILE TO FORCED UPLIFT ALONG THE GUST FRONT. FARTHER SW...ALTHOUGH CONVERGENCE/UPLIFT WILL BE WEAKER ALONG THE SRN FLANK OF THE ELONGATING COLD POOL THAT LIES MORE PARALLEL TO THE DEEP FLOW...THE PRESENCE OF A MORE FAVORABLE THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT /MUCAPE TO 1500 J PER KG WITH PW AROUND 1.50 INCHES/ SUGGESTS THAT STORM DEVELOPMENT WILL CONTINUE OVER SRN LWR MI. IN ADDITION...GLANCING INFLUENCE OF PROGRESSIVE UPR IMPULSE NOW CROSSING NRN LK MI WILL ENHANCE LARGE SCALE ASCENT OVER THE REGION. WHILE WIND PROFILES OVER SRN MI WILL BE AMPLE FOR STORM ORGANIZATION/SUSTENANCE...RELATIVELY WEAK LOW-LVL LAPSE RATES /GIVEN TIME OF DAY/ SUGGEST THAT ANY ASSOCIATED SVR THREAT IN THE NEAR TERM SHOULD REMAIN ISOLD AND NOT REQUIRE WW ISSUANCE. NEVERTHELESS...A WW MAY BE NEEDED LATER THIS MORNING FOR PARTS OF SRN MI IF AN INCREASE IN STORM COVERAGE/INTENSITY OCCUR WITH THE ONSET OF DAYTIME HEATING/LOW-LVL DESTABILIZATION. ..CORFIDI.. 08/07/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STRONG TO BRIEFLY SVR TSTMS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE OVER PARTS OF S CNTRL AND SE MO...BUT ADDITIONAL WW NOT EXPECTED. ADDITIONAL STORMS MAY INCREASE FARTHER SE INTO NE AR...WRN KY...AND TN.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STRONG TO BRIEFLY SVR TSTMS HAVE PERSISTED OVER S CNTRL AND SRN MO OVER THE PAST FEW HOURS IN THE ERN QUARTER OF WW 481...WHERE PROGRESSIVE PART OF MCS THAT MOVED EWD FROM KS INTERSECTED WNW-ESE BAND OF WAA STORMS OVER S CNTRL MO. MERGING OF THESE TWO AREAS OF ASCENT HAS RESULTED IN A FEW INSTANCES OF PRECIP-ENHANCED SFC WIND GUSTS AND SHORT-LIVED BOWING STRUCTURES. GIVEN HIGH PW /AROUND 2 INCHES/ AND CONTINUING PRESENCE OF 20-25 KT WNWLY DEEP SHEAR...POTENTIAL WILL PERSIST FOR ISOLD...LOCALLY SVR WIND GUSTS. A SIMILAR ENVIRONMENT EXTENDS ESE FROM THE ERN END OF WW 481 INTO WRN PARTS OF KY AND TN. SLIGHTLY ENHANCED SWLY LOW-LVL FLOW MAY SUPPORT SOME INCREASE IN STORM STRENGTH AND COVERAGE OVER THIS REGION DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS. HOWEVER...ATTM IT APPEARS THAT LOW-LVL LAPSE RATES AND NEAR-SFC FLOW WILL REMAIN TOO MARGINAL TO WARRANT AN ADDITIONAL WW IN THE NEAR-TERM. ELSEWHERE...LOW-LVL DESTABILIZATION IN TRAILING STRATIFORM PART OF MCS SUGGESTS THAT SVR THREAT HAS ENDED OVER THE REMAINDER OF WATCH 481 IN ERN KS AND W CNTRL/SW MO. ..CORFIDI.. 08/07/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...
